notes: Two exploratory runs (variable listing, seat-count and missingness checks; no RESULT lines), then one scored run. Specification taken from the paper text and the dataset codebooks: OLS with fixest, country-year (cntryyr) fixed effects, SEs clustered by cntryyr. Sample: directed dyads in dyadic_data_1-4-22.Rdata with to_prior_seats >= 4 and from_prior_seats >= 4 (the paper's 'at least four MPs each'; the 999 seat code, used only for the two US parties, passes the test), minus 44 dyads with missing to_pfeml. DV for columns 1-2 is party_like. For columns 3-4 it is 10 - dislike from gender_disagregated_8-8-21.rds (gender 2 = women, 1 = men), with the same seat filter. Regressors: to_pfeml; rile_distance_s, the CMP rile distance standardized over the full dataset (mean 22.44, SD 17.61, matching footnote 3); prior_coalition and prior_opposition, which the codebook lists as the variables used in the analysis (govern_together and opposition_together are marked 'not used'). n_election_studies counts the distinct cntryyr in the column-2 estimation sample. Judgment call: requiring only the out-party to have at least four seats would give a larger sample. I kept the paper's wording, which requires both parties to have at least four.
